sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 6.8% in FY2020 [D130], was flat at 0.2% growth in FY2023 [D284], then rose 125.9% in FY2024 [D338], 114.2% in FY2025 [D393] and 65.5% in FY2026 [D448].

The FY2024 step change came from Data Center revenue up 217% on Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P22][P23], and FY2025 growth was driven by Hopper demand with Blackwell production systems first shipping in the fourth quarter [P16].
FY2026 growth was driven by data center compute and networking platforms, with Blackwell architectures the majority of Data Center revenue [P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of revenue in FY2026 [D620], up from 19.9% in FY2018 [D598], and contributed 60.2pp of FY2026's growth [D622].
Within it, Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and Data Center networking grew 142% on the NVLink compute fabric ramp for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].

Networking contributed 14.1pp of FY2026 growth against 46.1pp from Compute [D636][D629]; the product members overlap on one axis and sum to 190% of consolidated revenue, so they are not additive [R2].
Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, at a 59.7% CAGR against 46.6% [F213][F211], and the incremental operating margin was 57.3% in FY2026 [D475].
Diluted EPS grew 66.7% in FY2026 against net income growth of 64.7% [D452][D450], with the diluted share count down 1.2% [D470].
Operating margin was 60.4% in FY2026 [F50], against a window median of 32.8% [D813], a high of 62.4% in FY2025 [D812] and a low of 15.7% in FY2023 [D811].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1% in FY2026 [F30][D462], with cost of revenue rising 91.4% against revenue growth of 65.5% [D465][D448].
The Compute & Networking operating income increase was partly offset by a $4.5 billion charge for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the first quarter of FY2026 [P7].
Operating expenses rose 40.7% [D468], driven by compensation and benefits from employee growth and by compute and infrastructure costs [P9].
Net margin held at 55.6% [F70] even as operating margin fell 2.0pp [D463], because other income of $11.1 billion [X120] lifted pre-tax income, and the effective tax rate rose to 15.1% [D434].
Operating cash flow was $102.7 billion and free cash flow $96.7 billion in FY2026 [F100][F110], a free-cash-flow margin of 44.8% [D432] against a window median of 44.4% [D822].
Operating cash flow covered net income 0.86 times [D435] and free cash flow covered net income 0.81x [D436], the low end of the FY2022..FY2026 range [D826].
Capex was $6.04 billion, 2.8% of revenue [F105][D431], and 2.13x D&A [D437], as inventory rose 112.3% and receivables 66.8% [D474][D473].
Cash used in investing activities rose to $52.2 billion [F120], primarily on higher purchases of equity investment securities and a non-exclusive license agreement with Groq [P1].
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion in FY2026 from $34.7 billion in FY2025 [D441][D386], as cash and investments dropped 75.5% to $10.6 billion [D471][D439] while total debt held at $8.47 billion [D440].

Net cash was still 1.0% of revenue [D442], in the 83rd percentile of six semis peers whose median is -13.9% [D844][D845], and the current ratio was 3.91x [F190] against a window median of 4.61x [D831].
Buybacks and dividends were $41.1 billion, 42.5% of free cash flow [D443][D444], with $40.1 billion of repurchases [X150] and $974 million of dividends [X160].
Acquisitions were $1.54 billion [X168] and goodwill rose to $20.8 billion from $5.19 billion [X252][X251].
Return on average equity was 101.5% [D447], in the 100th percentile of six peers against a 20.3% median [D848][D849].
Customer concentration is high: one direct customer was 22% of FY2026 revenue and another 14%, both primarily in Compute & Networking [P6].
China (including Hong Kong) revenue fell 21.4% in FY2026 and contributed -4.1pp to growth [D545][D546], cutting its share to 9.1% from 19.2% [D544][D541].
The Graphics segment's 25% revenue decline in FY2023 [D754], when it was 44.1% of revenue [D753], was a one-period event and has not recurred.
The concentration and China exposure matter because a single platform cycle now moves the whole company, and the filings do not explain the FY2026 China decline.
Gross margin: a further move below the FY2026 level of 71.1% [F30] would confirm the cost-of-revenue pressure seen in the 3.9pp decline [D462], reported in the FY2027 10-K.
Net cash: a fall below the FY2026 level of $2.14 billion [D441] would signal that investment purchases are outrunning cash generation, reported in the FY2027 10-K.
Data Center share: a move below the FY2026 level of 89.7% [D620] would mark the first diversification away from the AI platform, reported in the FY2027 10-K.
Cash conversion: operating cash flow below 0.86x net income [D435] would extend the multi-year drift down from the FY2020 level of 1.70x [D120].
